findings.evidence: dom-794.json contains no h1-h6 elements and no landmarks: the name "Elon Musk", the section titles (Summary, Experience, Open Source & Indie Work, Judgment & Conviction, Public Impact, Core Skills, Education) and the company names are all styled divs/spans.
findings.after: <h1> for the name, <h2> for each section title, <h3> for each company row head; the PDF export then carries tagged headings and bookmarks
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.3.1 Info and Relationships and 2.4.6 Headings and Labels (and PDF/UA tagging): a screen-reader user of the exported PDF gets one flat run of text with no way to jump between sections.
findings.title: Headings and landmarks
findings.fix: Fix levels in markup and size with CSS.

findings.where: Public Impact and writing/talks links, tile 2
findings.evidence: Link names do not match destinations: "@elonmusk" -> https://tesla.com/blog, "Master Plan Part Deux" -> https://youtube.com/ted, "First Principles Thinking in Engineering" -> https://spacex.com.
findings.after: Point each link at the item it names, or remove the <a> and keep plain text
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context): the accessible name must say where the link goes. Nearest curated card A11-006.
findings.title: Controls have accessible names

findings.title: No repeated labels inside a card

findings.where: inline emphasis in impact rows and skills, tiles 0-3
findings.evidence: Non-link phrases ("400+ launches", "7,000+ satellites", "7M+ vehicles delivered", "122 days", "first reusable orbital booster") are set in the same navy rgb(27,54,93) with no underline as the real links "SpaceX" and "Tesla"; neither is underlined.
findings.before: emphasis and links share color: rgb(27,54,93), no decoration
findings.after: Underline real links (text-decoration: underline; text-underline-offset: 2px) and render emphasis as font-weight: 600 in body ink
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.4.1 Use of Color: links must be distinguishable from surrounding text by more than colour; here colour also marks non-links, so a reader cannot tell which navy text is clickable in the PDF.
findings.title: Text contrast on real pixels
findings.fix: Darken text or lighten ground; never thin weights on tinted ground.

findings.where: metric row under the name, tile 0
findings.evidence: Four bare figures with no dates or sources: "30 yrs building hard tech", "6 cos founded / co-founded", "400+ Falcon launches", "7M+ Tesla vehicles". The sweep's stat_band did not fire (print profile). Later lines add more unsourced valuations: "Valued at $350B (2024)", "* $900B", "xAI valued at $50B".
findings.after: Date each figure and keep the source in a footnote ("Falcon 9 launches to [DATA NEEDED: as-of date], source: [DATA NEEDED]"), or drop the band; the experience rows already carry the numbers
findings.why: A résumé stat band of round, unsourced numbers is the slide-deck habit moved into a CV; it duplicates the body and cannot be checked.
findings.title: Stat bands need sources
findings.fix: Cite each figure, use supplied facts only, or remove the band.

findings.where: Experience timeline and xAI impact row, tiles 0-1
findings.evidence: Borrowed-authority lines that fail T-THREE-LINE (not falsifiable, attributed to no one): "Built physical infrastructure others called impossible.", "Colossus in 122 days, a pace the industry called implausible", "Every major OEM announced EV transition within 5 years of Model 3", "The industry assumption that rockets were expendable was gone within 24 months."
findings.after: State the fact and stop: "Colossus: 100K H100 GPUs, 122 days from concept to training."
findings.why: Unattributed 'others said it was impossible' framing is a model's way of adding drama; on a résumé it reads as puffery and undercuts the real figures beside it.

findings.evidence: The section heading promises open-source and indie work; its content is a philosophy line ("First-principles founder across hard tech. Approach: ..."), two company rows (SpaceX $350B, Tesla $900B) and a Falcon 9 landing callout. Its right-hand meta repeats the Experience meta ("1995 - present · Founder-engineer across six hard-tech companies"). "125 followers on GitHub" is the only open-source fact.
findings.after: Cut the section, or rename it to what it holds ("Approach") and drop the repeated company rows
findings.why: A template section kept and refilled with whatever fits shows the document was generated from a fixed skeleton, not from this person's material.
findings.title: Keep a true count from the client's set

findings.where: row labels ROLE / ACTIONS / IMPACT and Core Skills labels, tiles 0-3
findings.evidence: T-LABEL-TRANSFORM: 12px uppercase tracked navy labels repeat 12 times (ROLE/ACTIONS/IMPACT x4) and the skill labels wrap mid-phrase in caps ("CAPITAL · CRISIS / MGMT", "MANUFACTURING / · SCALE", with the middot starting a line).
